dedupe_keys.name: field wind speed measurements on a low rise building roof and pv array central washington university

description: This dataset gives wind speeds recorded by two ultrasonic anemometers on the roof of a low-rise building on the Central Washington University campus, in sparse suburban terrain. It was published on DesignSafe-CI in 2022 by Dorothy Reed, Greg Lyman, Johnny Estephan, Amanda Worthy, Arindam Gan Chowdhury, Shuoqi Wang and Peter Irwin, within an NSF project on peak wind loads on low-rise building envelopes and rooftop appurtenances such as photovoltaic arrays. One instrument sits at 21.9 m above ground on the roof and one in front of a PV array at 12.5 m; 15-minute time series were kept when mean wind speed exceeded 4.46 m/s, in CSV. Coverage: one building. Access: DesignSafe Data Depot, project PRJ-2470. Licence (read on the provider page on 2026-09-28): ODC-By-1.0. Access is free of charge. Caveats: the sampling rate is given as 'XX Hz' in the record. Simulation uses: comparing field turbulence with wind tunnel and full-scale tests for cladding and rooftop PV wind loads. Related records: the Harris County building population data and the NEES soft-story test.
